The framework integrates chatbots that have planning and reasoning capabilities, such as ChatGPT, with non-verbal instructions like pointing movements that enable users to directly manipulate images or videos on the screen. arxiv-2412-11314.title: Reliable, Reproducible, and Really Fast Leaderboards with Evalica
arxiv-2412-11314.creator: Dmitry Ustalov
arxiv-2412-11314.description: Abstract The rapid advancement of natural language processing (NLP) technologies, such as instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs), urges the development of modern evaluation protocols with human and machine feedback. We introduce Evalica , an open-source toolkit that facilitates the creation of reliable and reproducible model leaderboards.

arxiv-2503-17214.title: ML-Based Bidding Price Prediction for Pay-As-Bid Ancillary Services Markets: A Use Case in the German Control Reserve Market
arxiv-2503-17214.creator: Vincent Bezold 1, * Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation IPA, Nobelstraße 12, Stuttgart, 70569, Germany ORCID: 0009-0006-4430-4710 vincent.bezold@ipa.fraunhofer.de, Lukas Baur 1 Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation IPA, Nobelstraße 12, Stuttg
arxiv-2503-17214.description: Abstract The increasing integration of renewable energy sources has led to greater volatility and unpredictability in electricity generation, posing challenges to grid stability. Ancillary service markets, such as the German control reserve market, allow industrial consumers and producers to offer flexibility in their power consumption or generation, contributing to grid stability while earning additional income.

arxiv-2507-06267.title: Neural Network-Based Parameter Estimation for Non-Autonomous Differential Equations with Discontinuous Signals Thanks: Submitted to the editors, August 8, 2026.
arxiv-2507-06267.creator: Hyeontae Jo 1, 2, Krešimir Josić 3, 4, † \dagger, Jae Kyoung Kim 2, 5, † \dagger
arxiv-2507-06267.description: Abstract Non-autonomous differential equations are crucial for modeling systems influenced by external signals, yet fitting these models to data becomes particularly challenging when the signals change abruptly. To address this problem, we propose a novel parameter estimation method utilizing functional approximations with artificial neural networks.

arxiv-2507-12796.title: DeQA-Doc: Adapting DeQA-Score to Document Image Quality Assessment
arxiv-2507-12796.creator: Junjie Gao, Runze Liu, Yingzhe Peng, Shujian Yang, Jin Zhang, Kai Yang, Zhiyuan You, Ant Group, Southeast University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, CUHK, MBZUAI junjiegao19@gmail.com, {runze.liu, yingzhe.peng}@seu.edu.cn, thomasyang0925@sjtu.edu.cn{zj346862, chengyue.yk}@antgroup.com, zhiyuanyou@fo
arxiv-2507-12796.description: Abstract Document quality assessment is critical for a wide range of applications including document digitization, OCR, and archival. However, existing approaches often struggle to provide accurate and robust quality scores, limiting their applicability in practical scenarios. With the rapid progress in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), recent MLLM-based methods have achieved remarkable performance in image quality assessment.

plos-pone-0007172.description: PLOS ONE research article. While considerable evidence supports the causal relationship between increases in c-Myc (Myc) and cardiomyopathy as a part of a “fetal re-expression” pattern, the functional role of Myc in mechanisms of cardiomyopathy remains unclear. To address this, we developed a bitransgenic

pmc-10531268.title: Incidence and risk factors of graft-versus-host disease after liver transplantation: A national study 2010–2020
pmc-10531268.creator: Yuting Huang, Yichen Wang, R. Christopher Chase, Liu Yang
pmc-10531268.description: Background:Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a common complication of hematopoietic cell transplantation, and its incidence is low in liver transplantation (LT). Estimating the incidence of GVHD after LT is challenging due to the paucity of available data from the United Network for Organ Sharing. This is the first national analysis of the incidence and risk factors of GVHD after LT.

pmc-10567241.title: Is the association between financial scarcity and health behaviours moderated by cultural capital? The GLOBE study
pmc-10567241.creator: Sigrid L Oosterwegel, Nienke W Boderie, Frank J van Lenthe
pmc-10567241.description: BackgroundExperiencing financial scarcity taxes cognitive bandwidth. This leaves less capacity to withhold temptations and makes relying on easiest default options more likely. Whether this default option is (un)healthy may depend on the amount of cultural capital acquired during life course. This study examined whether the association between financial scarcity and health behaviours is moderated by cultural capital.

pmc-12474381.title: Norepinephrine Versus Dopamine as a First-Line Vasopressor in Dogs with Hypotension: A Pilot Study
pmc-12474381.creator: Bridget Lyons, Rebecka Hess, Deborah C Silverstein, Lian Li
pmc-12474381.description: Simple SummaryDiseases that cause severe inflammation can result in a decrease in blood pressure. If not treated appropriately, inadequate blood delivery to the major organs of the body can cause damage or failure. In addition to treating the underlying cause of severe inflammation, medical therapy to increase the low blood pressure is often administered.

pmc-12511426.title: Micro-nano microbial fuel cell-driven bioelectrochemical tumor therapy
pmc-12511426.creator: Ruiyan Li, Yong Kang, Nana Ran, Gaoli Niu, Yueyue Fan, Yijing Zhang, Jiamin Ye, Xue Yuan, Jiacheng Shi, Mengbin Ding, Yuhan Zhang, Xiaoyuan Ji
pmc-12511426.description: Colorectal cancer remains one of the most challenging malignancies to treat due to its intestinal physiological barrier, extracellular interstitial barrier, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here we develop a micro-nano microbial fuel cell system, integrating Desulfovibrio desulfuricans (Dsv) as a biological electron donor and MnO2 as a catalytic electron acceptor, to achieve bioelectrochemical tumor modulation.

pmc-12627888.title: Statistical innovations in clinical trial design with a focus on drug combinations, factorials, and other multiple therapy issues
pmc-12627888.creator: Donald A Berry
pmc-12627888.description: Statistical methods in clinical research tend to become entrenched. Innovations threaten the status quo. The “right way” becomes frozen in lore. This is so even when the “right way” is not best. “Statistical significance” and the associated requirement of “high power” is an example. This attitude is an impediment to efficient design.

pmc-12975943.title: The SIRP family: from structural diversity and signaling mechanisms to implications in immune-related disease targeted therapeutics
pmc-12975943.creator: Yanmei Jin, Quiyang Huang, Jiaqi Song, Zain ul Abideen, Ruijiong Tan, Shaohua Xu, Ming Chen
pmc-12975943.description: Signal regulatory proteins (SIRPs) are membrane receptors on immune cells that control immune homeostasis and inflammation. Although SIRP family members share homologous extracellular domains, they differ in intracellular motifs and function: SIRPα transduces inhibitory signals, SIRPβ associates with DAP12 to trigger activation, and SIRPγ primarily modulates adhesion and T cell responses.

pmc-13145426.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2039 THE INTERSECTION OF RACE/ETHNICITY, SEX AND EDUCATION AND STROKE RISK
pmc-13145426.creator: Lynda Lisabeth, Madeline Kwicklis, Xu Shi, Christopher Becker, Lewis Morgenstern
pmc-13145426.description: Background and aimsDisparities in stroke risk by race/ethnicity, sex, and socioeconomic status are well documented; however, most prior research has examined these factors independently rather than jointly. Our objective was to assess how the intersection of race/ethnicity, sex, and educational attainment influences stroke risk.MethodsFirst-ever ischemic strokes (n=3,401) were identified from a population-based study conducted in south Texas, USA (2012–2019, 2021–2023).

pmc-13199430.title: Qualitative EEG abnormalities in ASD reflect inhibition-dominated brain dynamics
pmc-13199430.creator: Arthur-Ervin Avramiea, Erika L. Juarez-Martinez, Pilar Garcés, Joerg F. Hipp, Simon-Shlomo Poil, Marina Diachenko, Huibert D. Mansvelder, Emily Jones, Luke Mason, Declan Murphy, Eva Loth, Bethany Oakley, Tony Charman, Tobias Banaschewski, Bob Oranje, Jan Buitelaar, Hilgo Bruining, Klaus Linkenkaer-H
pmc-13199430.description: Qualitative EEG abnormalities are common in Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and hypothesized to reflect disrupted excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. To test this, we recently introduced a functional measure of network-level E/I ratio (fE/I). Here, we applied fE/I and other EEG measures to alpha oscillations from source-reconstructed data in the EU-AIMS dataset (267 ASD, 209 controls).

pmc-13201971.title: Occipital transtentorial approach selected based on venous anatomy for a vermian cavernous malformation: illustrative case
pmc-13201971.creator: Mizuto Sato, Akimitsu Shirokihara, Natsumi Ogawa, Takaki Ichikawa, Takahiro Miyata, Masashi Nakatsukasa, Joji Inamasu
pmc-13201971.description: BACKGROUNDCavernous malformations of the superior cerebellar vermis beneath the tentorium are rare and surgically challenging because approach selection must account for lesion location and venous anatomy.OBSERVATIONSA 69-year-old man presented with vertigo, nausea, and truncal ataxia caused by hemorrhage from a cavernous malformation of the superior cerebellar vermis.

pmc-13355843.title: Exosome-Mediated Macrophage Polarization in Gastric Cancer: Inflammatory and Neuroinflammatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential
pmc-13355843.creator: Wei An, Ze Jin, Yan Li
pmc-13355843.description: Gastric cancer progression is driven by intricate crosstalk among exosomes, macrophage polarization, inflammatory dysregulation, and tumor-associated neuroinflammation within the tumor microenvironment, which collectively form a reciprocal vicious cycle. As critical intercellular mediators, exosomes derived from tumor cells, immune cells, and stem cells deliver microRNA cargos to orchestrate M1/M2 macrophage balance and modulate neuroinflammatory states, exerting either pro-tumor or anti-tumor effects.

pmc-13382014.title: Conceptual replication and validation of the PACER survey in the multi-ethnic study of atherosclerosis (MESA)
pmc-13382014.creator: Yvonne L Michael, Kari Moore, Reyhaneh A Yazdi, Jana A Hirsch
pmc-13382014.description: ObjectiveThe Perceptions About Changes in Environments and Residents (PACER) survey was developed to measure individual experiences of health-related neighborhood gentrification. Initial validation in Philadelphia and Montreal supported its reliability and validity, but generalizability remained limited by geographic and demographic constraints.

pmc-13405731.title: Safety Profile of Intranasal Corticosteroids in Allergic Rhinitis: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-13405731.creator: Mirko Maglica, Franko Batinović, Marin Gudelj, Braco Bošković, Ivan Mizdrak, Stjepan Radić, Marta Knežević, Ivan Paladin
pmc-13405731.description: Intranasal corticosteroids (INCS) remain the cornerstone of pharmacologic treatment for allergic rhinitis (AR) because of their well-established anti-inflammatory efficacy and generally favorable benefit–risk profile. Nevertheless, concerns regarding local and systemic corticosteroid-related adverse events (AEs) continue to influence patient adherence, prescribing practices, and long-term treatment acceptance.
